notes: A clean six-bullet avatar quest with two real evidence points, so the ladder is genuinely trackable end to end. 'Previous' is empty but 'Quest Reqs: Darkness Named' is a quest title, so that is what prev records -- the header simply put the prerequisite in the other field. The red-ruled block between bullets 2 and 3 is the long way in for players without the Pso'Xja Home Point (Beaucedine Glacier (H-8), displacements red-purple-red-purple, elevator, the Stone Gate that eats the Pso'Xja pass key item); it is one conditional route, not four steps, so it lives in step 2's note. Pso'Xja (9) and The Shrouded Maw (10) are two different zones and the page walks you from one into the other, so they are two travel steps. The whole of bullet 5's spell list and the vanishing-tile warning is battle advice. The 'After the walkthrough: Notes' section is six party/limit/cooldown facts and contributes no steps: party size, the per-member vial, the 30 minute limit, one reward at a time, once per Earth day, and a first-clear cutscene that varies with CoP progress. The once-per-Earth-day repeat is invisible to the addon.

steps.note: Windurst Waters South is the south half of zone 238, not a zone of its own. Home Point #3 is just south of her. Every party member needs their own vial.

the page assumes Pso'Xja Home Point #1. Without it: Beaucedine Glacier (H-8) (the Survival Guide lands at H-9), then displacements red - purple - red - purple, elevator down, north then west, and the Stone Gate consumes a Yes on the Pso'Xja pass key item. Every displacement strips all buffs, Trusts included.
down the steps from Pso'Xja; a separate zone, which is why it is a separate rung
pick 'Waking Dreams' from the menu. The vial is what gets you in, so it is listed as held here even though bullet 4 does not restate it.
up to 6, 30 minute limit, no Trust Magic. The floor tiles vanish during the fight and drop you into Diremites.
one reward only per clear -- the avatar, one of four pieces of gear, or 15,000 gil -- so none of them is evidence of anything but the quest being over

notes:
Nine bullets, four steps. Bullets 2 and 3 are the same conversation as bullet 1 -- accepting the offer and being given map markers is not a second visit to Mapitoto -- so they merge into step 1. Bullets 5, 6 and 8 are all commentary on the one course in bullet 4: the motivation bar, /cheer at 50%, the retry-on-failure prompt, and a worked route (J-8 - I-7 - H-6 - G-6 - F-7 - E-6) whose grids confirm the course runs in Batallia Downs. The walkthrough never names the zone, but the header Description does ('head to Batallia Downs. Seek out Syrillia'), so it is the page's own name and not an invention. The five foods are never named and nothing observable counts them, so step 2 has no items and no evidence -- an unnamed, uncountable fetch is exactly the shape that must stay a bare rung. The header's Quest Reqs are two key items rather than a quest, and both resolve, so they ride on step 1 as things you must hold. Raptor companion IS the reward and does not resolve as a key item anyway, so the turn-in has no evidence. The 'Repeating the Quest' section is a title-chasing time trial, not extra steps: sub-4-minute completion at the original difficulty, which nothing in the packets can see; header Repeatable is empty, so this stays false.

Moved out of the player-facing step notes (build vocabulary; see AUTHORING.md, 'Two notes, two audiences'):
  step 4: but it is the reward, and it does not resolve against res/key_items.lua either, so it is not used as evidence

steps.note: any job at level 20+, so the level gate is not a job gate. Rusese at the M&P Market nearby sells the map for 500 gil. Accepting the offer and having the feeding points marked on your map (Map > Markers) is the same conversation, not a second step.

five feeds, mounted, against a depleting motivation bar. The page never names the food, so there is nothing to hold and nothing to count; the marked points show under the green NPC markers and each throws a pillar of light, with the food inside a burrow -- go round the mound for the rectangular entryway. Uphill drains motivation fast; /cheer at 50%+ tops it up. Failure ('Run off into the sunset...') offers a retry, optionally at a lower difficulty.
stay mounted when you talk to her; she warps you back
You get the Raptor companion key item directly rather than a Raptor Mount item.

notes: The walkthrough opens by saying the quest starts automatically on finishing Chasing Shadows, so nobody is ever talked to to begin it -- the header's Bostillette, Batallia Downs (S) is kept verbatim as the start because she resolves and it costs nothing, but the first thing a player actually does is zone into Jugner Forest, which is why the flag is set. Bullets 4 and 5 are one object examined twice in one place (cutscene, then battlefield), the Divine Might shape, so they are one rung. The Orcish infiltration kit is recorded as step 3's evidence and NOT as a requirement of the Scrape Mark: the page never says you hand it over, only that spares are sold by Clandestine Marking, so requiring it would be my inference rather than the page's claim. Bullets 7, 8 and 9 are battle tactics; only bullet 6 ('you only need to kill Fangmonger Colossus') decides what the fight step is, so the six Tombstones stay in the note rather than becoming six kill markers on optional adds. The instruction to examine the Cavernous Maw is in an UNNUMBERED line before bullet 10 -- bullets 10 and 11 are its caveat and its shortcut -- so that is what step 6 cites. Bullet 12 is a genuine conditional branch (full inventory only) and is optional; the ??? it names cannot carry a marker but keeps its rung. Bullet 13 is a Trust unlock that outlives the quest, and the closing line about Adieu, Lilisette is a mission cross-reference; neither is a step.

the cutscene is on zoning in. Ways there: Domenic in Lower Jeuno (J-7) for 750 gil if you have cleared Beyond Infinity, the Fort Ghelsba Survival Guide next door, or Home Point to Yughott Grotto and Escape. Spare kits from Clandestine Marking at (I-10).

Map 1, in from Ghelsba Outpost. Examine twice: the first is a cutscene, the second enters the battlefield Face of the Future. Do not draw your weapon at the entrance -- that starts the fight from any distance.

the Colossus alone ends it. Six Tombstones share the field and each one killed drops its damage resistance, but they are optional and respawn, so they are not recorded as kill targets. Excenmille and Maxcimille start with you and Bostillette joins partway. Everything is statue-slow and kites easily; Seismostomp and the conal paralysis Numbing Glare are the moves to watch.

the instruction itself is the unnumbered line after bullet 9; bullets 10 and 11 are its conditions. This maw must already have been unlocked from the past or the cutscene will not play, and the Batallia Downs Survival Guide is the quick way. The Griffon Ring arrives here, but it is the header's reward, not evidence.
only if your inventory was full during the final cutscene: make space, then examine the ??? near the maw on the past side to collect the Griffon Ring. A ??? can never carry a marker.

notes:
Twelve bullets and almost all of them are real: a five-evidence ladder, which is about as trackable as a CoP-era quest gets. The two Item Reqs sit on the steps that spend them (garlic to Muckvix, one tear to Tarnotik) rather than on the quest as a whole. Step 5 is the one gate I cannot express: Magriffon wants 10,000 gil, and gil is not an item, so items is empty and the requirement is a note -- both key items it grants are still evidence, and they are granted together in one cutscene so they are one AND-list on one step. Step 8's tear has a genuine alternative -- the page says you can skip bringing tears if you have the Home Point warp, though you must still have talked to Tarnotik -- which is exactly what items_partial is for. Bullets 7 and 8 are the same NPC back to back and stay two rungs because the page really does make them two visits with a zone-and-retry caveat between them. The Orcs that drop Misareaux Garlic are never named as a mob, so step 3 records no mobs rather than inventing one. Bullet 12 is the page's own 'Optional followup' and Ravorara's location is never given, so that step has no zone. The 'After the walkthrough: Boss Fight' section is two facts and a table about Twilotak -- unrestricted now, no Trusts, three Moblin Wisewomen and three Moblin Clergymen who buff but do not attack and need not die -- all of which is battle detail folded into step 10's note, not steps.

Moved out of the player-facing step notes (build vocabulary; see AUTHORING.md, 'Two notes, two audiences'):
  step 8: the tear is the taxi to Mine Shaft #2716 and every member of the party needs one. items_partial because the Home Point warp replaces the tear entirely

notes: The header's Start is empty and the walkthrough never names a giver -- Voidwatch operations are handed to you by the previous quest -- so start is null throughout rather than guessed. That is survivable here only because several later steps resolve as markable entities; nothing else in this batch depends on it. Bullets 1 and 3 are each a set of six battles the page lists as one item, and nothing orders them, so each becomes six steps sharing a group ('tier1', 'tier2') with its own zone: twelve rungs that all draw at once, which is what 'complete the 6' actually means. Every one of them has three possible spawn points in its zone, so grid stays null and the three go in the note -- a single grid would be a lie two thirds of the time. The Crawlers' Nest (S) entry names two mobs separated by a slash, so both are recorded with a note that only one appears. Step 7's abyssite upgrade is the only clean evidence in the quest: hold White stratum abyssite, come back holding II. The Voidwatch Officer of bullet 4 is deliberately NOT recorded as a target: the name is on the addon's ambiguous list and the page gives no zone ('any Voidwatch Officer, past or present'), and an ambiguous NPC with no zone is a structural failure that would collapse this whole quest to start-only -- which, with no start NPC, means nothing at all. The rung and its Voidwatch alarum evidence survive; only the marker is lost. Bullet 5's rewards are all in the header Reward list, so neither the abyssite III nor the emblem is evidence. The Bulwark Gate is the page's own '(Optional-ish)' and is marked optional, with its warning to do it before A World in Flux kept in the note.
